masteryZone.q: Which memory is the absolute fastest in the hierarchy?
masteryZone.sol: CPU Registers are fastest, operating at processor core speed.

masteryZone.q: Which cache level is shared among all CPU cores?
masteryZone.sol: L3 Cache is typically shared among all CPU cores on the chip.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Cache memory operates based on the Locality of Reference principle.
masteryZone.sol: True. Cache relies on spatial and temporal locality to load active variables.

masteryZone.q: What semiconductor RAM type is used to build cache memory?
Which RAM requires constant electrical refreshing?
masteryZone.sol: DRAM uses capacitors which lose charge and require continuous refreshing.

masteryZone.q: Which ROM is erased using Ultraviolet (UV) light?
masteryZone.sol: EPROM is erased by UV light exposure through its quartz window.

masteryZone.q: True or False: EEPROM chips can be erased electrically byte-by-byte.
masteryZone.sol: True. EEPROM stands for Electrically Erasable Programmable ROM, allowing byte-level writes.

masteryZone.q: What volatile RAM serves as system main memory?
What is the data storage capacity of a standard CD?
masteryZone.sol: A standard CD has a capacity of 700 MB.

masteryZone.q: Which measurement unit is equal to 1024 Gigabytes (GB)?
True or False: A single Nibble consists of 8 binary bits.
masteryZone.sol: False. A Nibble consists of 4 bits; a Byte consists of 8 bits.
